cost: Cholesky O(n³), triangular O(n²), QR O(m*n²), stationary O(k*n²); O(m*n+n²) inputs/work; n<=64,m<=128,iterations<=10000.
description: Factor bounded symmetric systems, solve triangular systems, minimize linear least squares and iterate linear solves with fresh residuals.
forward: Factor bounded symmetric systems, solve triangular systems, minimize linear least squares and iterate linear solves with fresh residuals.
Cholesky A=L*Lᵀ transports b through lower and upper solves. QR normal equations transport least squares to a quadratic. Stationary solvers share Ax=b but not trajectories.
inverse: At the real-model level, exclude nontriangular Cholesky factors or A!=L*Lᵀ, triangular solutions with T*x!=b, and least-squares candidates with Aᵀ(A*x-b)!=0. These exact exclusions describe targets, not an exact-equality acceptance test for f64 outputs. The native relation excludes reports differing from rounded factor/solve transitions, incorrect recomputed reconstruction/primal/normal residuals, or a stationary Converged status when its computed residual exceeds tolerance. A small native residual does not exclude large coordinate error on ill-conditioned inputs; numerical rank is not certified by unpivoted QR.

For fixed real triangular T and observed x, compatible right sides satisfy b=T*x; allowing T to vary gives many systems with the same solution. For fixed full-column-rank A, the real QR least-squares fiber for x is b=A*x+z with Aᵀz=0, so nonzero orthogonal residuals remain compatible. A real positive-diagonal Cholesky factor uniquely determines A=L*Lᵀ, while rounded native factor/report fibers can include neighboring matrices. Stationary output plus residual/status leaves many initial vectors, budgets and systems compatible; native antecedents must reproduce the rounded execution, not merely these real identities.
limitations: Positive pivots in floating arithmetic do not certify spectral conditioning. Unpivoted QR rejects exact zero encountered pivots only. Stationary convergence requires matrix properties not inferred from finite success.
Finite tests and source-derived models are not a universal proof.
state: Dimensions and coordinates agree; residual, reconstruction residual and normal residual are different observations; explicit errors/statuses retained.
